cards.text: Friend, this message is from the prophet Isaiah, and it's about Zion, another name for Jerusalem. It opens with a voice that flat out REFUSES to quit: "For Zion’s sake I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not keep still…" Some people talk when they're nervous, but this voice talks until something CHANGES.

cards.question: This voice won't keep still for Jerusalem's sake. How long does it keep going?

answers.text: Until her righteousness shines like a bright light
Until her enemies scatter like dust in the wind
Until her walls stand strong like a mighty fortress

cards.text: When it shines, nations will see her righteousness, and all kings her glory. Friend, this isn't a night-light in the hallway, this is the house on the block whose Christmas lights you can see from the HIGHWAY.

cards.question: Zion will also be called by a new name. Who gives it to her?

cards.text: Then the picture gets royal. Zion will be a crown of glory, a royal diadem.

cards.question: Zion, this crown of glory, is held by the LORD.

cards.text: Right there in the hand of the LORD, a royal diadem in the palm of her God. Now, the names she's been called: Forsaken, and her land, Desolate.

cards.question: Zion will go on being called Forsaken.

cards.text: Instead, she'll be called Hephzibah, and her land Beulah. Friend, I practiced saying Hephzibah THREE times before I said it out loud, and I STILL said it like I was asking a question.

cards.question: Why will Zion be called Hephzibah?

answers.text: The LORD will take delight in her
Her people will finally deserve it
Her old name will be forgotten

cards.text: Her land will be His bride, and as a young man marries a young woman, so her sons will marry her. Now picture the groom when the doors open and the bride walks in, friend: that man is GONE, grinning like nobody else is even in the room.

cards.question: Like a bridegroom with his bride, Zion's God will ___ over her.

cards.text: Now we're up on the walls of Jerusalem. Watchmen have been posted there.

cards.question: The watchmen on Jerusalem's walls get to go quiet at night.

cards.text: Never silent, day or night, like a group chat you leave for TEN minutes and come back to 200 messages. And those who call on the LORD are told to take no rest, and to give Him no rest either.

cards.question: Those who call on the LORD keep at it until what happens?

answers.text: He makes Jerusalem the praise of the earth
The watchmen come down off the walls
The harvest is brought in at last

cards.text: Then the LORD swears an oath, by His right hand and by His mighty arm.

cards.question: The LORD swears something will never happen to Zion again. What is it?

cards.text: No more foreigners drinking the new wine Zion toiled for, either. Back in the Millers' kitchen I'd turn around and half a batch was GONE off the cooling rack, so friend, I feel this one.

cards.question: Those who harvest Zion's grain will eat it and praise the LORD.

cards.text: And those who gather grapes will drink the wine in the LORD's holy courts. Then the voice gets LOUD: go out through the gates, build up the highway, clear away the stones, raise a banner for the nations!

cards.question: Who is this highway being prepared for?

cards.text: And the LORD has proclaimed something to the ends of the earth. It's a message for Daughter Zion.

cards.question: What's the big news the LORD proclaims for Daughter Zion?
When Zion's Savior comes, He comes empty-handed.

cards.text: And look at the names now. They will be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of the LORD.

cards.question: And Zion will be called Sought Out, A City Not ___.

cards.text: Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know what a name like that means.

findings.problem: Card 1 quotes the first half of Isaiah 62:1 and stops at 'keep still…'. Card 2 then asks the baker to supply the rest of that same line ('until her righteousness shines like a bright light'). That is guessing the next words of a line, not reasoning about movement or meaning. Card 1 only says 'until something CHANGES', so the pick comes down to wording.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The joke describes a groom 'grinning like nobody else is even in the room' when the bride walks in. That already tells the baker the bridegroom rejoices, which gives away the 'rejoice' blank on card 12 and rules out 'watch' and 'weep'. Card 12 asks what Zion's God does 'like a bridegroom with his bride'.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Isaiah 62:9 says 'those who harvest grain will eat it and praise the LORD'. It never says whose grain. The card adds 'Zion's grain', which settles who is meant where the verse leaves it open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This last story card repeats 'Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken', the answer card 15 just gave, and adds a personal line. It tells no new part of the passage, so it works as a recap card.

Each stop has exactly one fill-in-the-blank card, and in both stops it is the last choice card (stop 1 card 12, stop 2 card 15). Where the blank falls repeats across the stops instead of being chosen naturally.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Card 1 quotes a speaker using 'I' ('I will not keep silent… I will not keep still') and calls it only 'a voice'. Isaiah 62:1 does not say whether the speaker is the LORD or the prophet. Two rules point different ways. papa-dorin.md says that when he quotes an 'I' speaker 'he says who it is first'. The Scripture rules say to leave open what the text leaves open. The opening card is also meant to say who is speaking.
findings.question: When a passage quotes an 'I' speaker the text doesn't identify, as in Isaiah 62:1 and 62:6, should Papa Dorin leave the speaker unnamed ('a voice')? Or should he name the most likely speaker, or say the speaker isn't named?
